summary: Cook County, MN summit tower built 1946 per a Superior NF brochure, about 35 feet tall; torn down mid-1960s; now a hiking-only day-use area of Temperance River State Park.

facts.status_note: Removed; the 2004 survey mark recovery found the tower gone and base remnants visible

visit.trail_note: Hiking only, about 3 miles round trip from the Britton Peak trailhead, 550-foot elevation gain (2004 brochure)

notes_for_editor: The 1946 build date and the builders' names come from one brochure; no other source read gives a build year. Tower type is unclear: the A-Z list calls it a ladder and stair tower with a square cab, while the 1952 survey text says steel with four legs; the story uses the survey wording. The brochure is dated 2004; the current state of the peak is taken from Wikipedia. Removal year is approximate. A Cook County Historical Society Facebook post mentions a lookout worker at the Carlton Peak tower; the page did not load, so it is not used. Agency in the brief (Superior National Forest) is kept; the peak is now state park land.
